title: II–VII: definition; essential parts — body and rational immortal spirit
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): yet through himself he is an essence lacking body — although this spirit dwells in ye body. VII. Revelation 6:9 — 1 Thessalonians 5:23 — 2 Corinthians 5; 12:2 — Acts 7:59 — Matthew 10:28 — Zechariah 12:1 — Genesis 2:7 — powerful with intellect plus will, so united toward ye human body that nevertheless he can be separated out from it — ye invisible part belonging toward humankind. VI. Ye rational plus immortal SPIRIT is. Genesis 2:7; Job 10:11; Matthew 6:25; 1 Corinthians 12:12 — a fleshy structure supported by bones plus covered by skin, animated by breath — ye visible part belonging toward him. V. Ye human BODY is. IV. His essential parts are ye animated body plus ye rational spirit. III. But in humankind there are to be considered both essential parts, plus sex, plus finally proper affections. Acts 17:28; 1 Corinthians 11:7 — Ecclesiastes 7:29 — Genesis 1:26-27; 9:6 — we here considering him in order toward his creation have described him out from ye biblical text. briefly indeed plus in philosophical manner humankind is defined a rational animal. according toward His likeness toward ye image belonging toward God — endowed with immortal rational spirit — made a living soul by breath into his nostrils — made by GOD through ye Word out from ye dust belonging toward earth. II. Humankind is ye last belonging toward creatures.
pass_b_english: II. Humankind is the last of creatures, made by GOD through the Word from the dust of the earth, and by breath into his nostrils made a living soul, endowed with immortal rational spirit according to the image of God after His likeness. Briefly and in the philosophical manner humankind is defined a rational animal; we here, considering him in order to his creation, have described him from the biblical text — Genesis 1:26–27; 9:6; Ecclesiastes 7:29; Acts 17:28; 1 Corinthians 11:7.

III. In humankind there are to be considered essential parts, sex, and finally proper affections. IV. His essential parts are the animated body and the rational spirit. V. The human BODY is his visible part, a fleshy structure supported by bones and covered by skin, animated by breath — Genesis 2:7; Job 10:11; Matthew 6:25; 1 Corinthians 12:12. VI. The rational and immortal SPIRIT is the invisible part of humankind, powerful with intellect and will, so united to the human body that nevertheless it can be separated from it — Genesis 2:7; Zechariah 12:1; Matthew 10:28; Acts 7:59; 2 Corinthians 5; 12:2; 1 Thessalonians 5:23; Revelation 6:9. VII. This spirit, though it dwells in the body, is through itself an essence without body.
source_text: II. Homo est creaturarum ultima a DEO λόγῳ facta de pulvere terrae, sufflatuque in nares ipsius facta anima vivens, spiritu rationali immortali praedita ad imaginem Dei secundum similitudinem ipsius. Breviter quidem et philosophico more finitur homo animal rationale; nos hic eum in ordine ad creationem suam considerantes descripsimus e textu biblico Gen. I.26–27; IX.6; Eccl. VII.29; Act. XVII.28; 1 Cor. XI.7. III. Sunt autem in homine considerandae tum partes essentiales, tum sexus, tum denique affectiones propriae. IV. Ejus partes essentiales sunt corpus animatum et spiritus rationalis. V. CORPUS humanum est pars illius visibilis, structura carnea, ossibus fulta et cute contecta, sufflatu animata — Gen. II.7; Job. X.11; Matth. VI.25; 1 Cor. XII.12. VI. SPIRITUS rationalis et immortalis est pars hominis invisibilis, intellectu et voluntate pollens, corpori humano ita unitus ut tamen ab eo separari possit — Gen. II.7; Zach. XII.1; Matth. X.28; Act. VII.59; 2 Cor. V; XII.2; 1 Thess. V.23; Apoc. VI.9. VII. Hic spiritus, quamvis in corpore habitet, per se tamen est essentia corporis expers.
